title: Clearing an item's named source root makes its next turn fall back to the main workspace, which the host records as a source change that stales the item's passing evaluation
outcome: After an own-clear of an item's named source root, or any root release, the next turn's fallback workspace is never attributed to the item as a source change (no assumed-missing-baseline mutation); any staleness of the pre-clear evaluation comes only from Engram's existing named-root binding rule and is explained as such. Owed source-accounting duties captured before the clear are preserved, held and diagnosed locally; canonical completion protection for them is tracked separately as a cross-project dependency.
acceptance: A regression covers: name a root, record a passing evaluation on source S, own-clear the root, then run one more turn of the same claim whose session workdir is a different workspace. No source_changed:true with assumed_missing_baseline, and no other source-mutation observation, is attributed to the item for the fallback workspace. Any refusal or staleness of the pre-clear evaluation comes only from Engram's existing named-root binding rule (an explicit clear, release or rename ends that binding), is reported as such and not as a source mutation, and the fix neither disables nor bypasses that rule. The regression and any live check name the exact Engram version they ran against.

A genuine source change observed after evaluation while the evaluated root remains the captured source scope still stales the evaluation. A newly named root with different content is measured and does not reuse the old evaluation as current. Confirmed clear/release ends future automatic source observation for that claim until another root is named; it does not assert that the old tree is unchanged and does not discard already captured accounting or carried-check duties: an owed closing observation retained across clear/release is preserved durably, held from provider delivery with an explicit historical-recovery diagnosis, and never presented as unchanged or as accounted, and canonical completion protection for such a duty is explicitly not established by this item and is tracked as a cross-project dependency. Completion with a truthfully supplied different source fingerprint refuses the old evaluation. Regressions cover the bound-root change, owed close preserved and held across clear/reload (including an excursion and revert), re-naming with different content, and the distinction between no post-clear observation and completion-fingerprint mismatch.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact committed tree, with a clean independent review pair.
